root.name: Sicilian Defense: Kan Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 a6

overview: Black plays ...a6 and ...e6 to keep a flexible set-up, aiming for ...Qc7, ...b5, ...Bb7 or ...Nc6 and ...d6, delaying committing the king's knight. White usually plays 5.Nc3 Qc7 6.Bd3 or 6.Be2, or 5.c4 for the Maróczy bind. Black hits the centre via ...b5-b4 and ...d5, with queenside counterplay and a hidden attacking potential.

white_ideas.idea: Bd3, O-O and Qe2 or f4 for a kingside attack against the Kan set-up

typical_structures.structure: Sicilian with e6/d6 or a6/b5 against White e4/d4 or c4/e4 bind

character.notes: Sicilian with rich tactical chances, flexible, with attacks on both wings; a miss lets either side get hit.

structure.notes: Every Sicilian is semi-open: c-file for Black.

level.notes: Flexible; plans are subtle but there is less long theory than Najdorf.

character.reason: Open Sicilian with opposite plans and attacking chances for both.

structure.reason: Every Sicilian is semi-open per the rubric.

level.reason: Flexible move order but modest forced theory.

plans.reason: Black plays on the c-file and expands with ...b5.
